chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who catches the end of the Imam’s salat, while it is the beginning of the man’s salat, and he does not give him time to recite; should he then make up the recitation at the end of his salat?

His statement, 'he makes up the recitation at the end of his salat,' is figurative usage. What is meant by it is that which pertains to the end of the salat of the recitation of al-Ḥamd, not that he intended by it making up the recitation of what pertains specifically to the first and second rakʿah.

key_terms.آخِرِ صَلَاتِهِ: the latter part of his prayer
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat

ai.seo_question: If someone joins the Imam late and misses recitation, does he make up the qirāʾah at the end of his salat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who joins the Imam late in congregational salat and misses the opportunity to recite at the start of his own prayer. It explains that reciting later in the prayer is described figuratively as 'making up' the recitation, meaning the recitation appropriate to that later part of the salat, not a literal replacement of what belongs specifically to the first two rakʿahs.
